title: artemisia seriphium var. gallica
intro: Artemisia seriphium var. gallica, commonly known as Roman Wormwood, is a variety of the wormwood plant native to Europe and Asia. It has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, which include treating digestive issues and relieving anxiety and stress due to its health benefits. The plant exhibits therapeutic actions such as anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiseptic properties, making it effective in wound healing and as an antiparasitic agent. The bioactive constituents of Roman Wormwood include essential oils containing thujone, sesquiterpenes, and flavonoids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
